short: Thirty-one days in office, and the first test of what happens when a president dies.
full:
Harrison was elected in 1840 on a campaign of log cabins and hard cider that said almost nothing about policy. On 4 March 1841, aged 68 and bareheaded in cold rain, he delivered the longest inaugural address ever given: 8,445 words, nearly two hours. He fell ill three weeks later and died on 4 April, the first president to die in office.

The Constitution was ambiguous about whether the vice president assumed the office itself or only its powers. John Tyler settled the question unilaterally by taking the oath, moving into the White House, and returning unopened any mail addressed to him as acting president. Congress grumbled and acquiesced, and the precedent held through seven further deaths in office until the Twenty-fifth Amendment wrote it into law in 1967. Harrison's term remains the shortest in American history.
